title: Decide what to do with pre-existing unstaged WIP
description:
Throughout the 2026-05-12 session, the following files have been sitting as pre-existing unstaged changes, untouched per explicit instruction:

  modified:   .beads/config.yaml
  modified:   .beads/metadata.json
  modified:   AGENTS.md
  modified:   CLAUDE.md

Plus an untracked OLD/ directory (probably draft snapshots).

The instruction during the session was 'leave the pre-existing unstaged edits to AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or .beads/* — those are unrelated work-in-progress.' But unrelated WIP that sits indefinitely is itself a state to manage.

Possible decisions:
- Commit them with whatever commit message describes the change (if Mark remembers what they were)
- Stash them if not ready to commit
- Discard them with git checkout if they were experimental and aren't wanted
- Leave them indefinitely (the current state)

The .beads/ working state has accumulated more changes from this session's bead creation activity, so the .beads/ files now contain a mix of session-relevant and pre-session changes. Untangling that may require some care.

This bead is a reminder, not a directive. Mark decides.
acceptance_criteria:
- Each of AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, and the .beads/ files has a recorded decision (committed, stashed, discarded, or explicit 'leave indefinitely')
- If 'leave indefinitely' is chosen, the bead's close-reason states the policy so subsequent sessions don't waste cycles re-evaluating
- The OLD/ directory similarly has a decision (gitignored, deleted, or left untracked indefinitely)
close_reason: All three pre-existing WIP items resolved in same session: OLD/ discarded, AGENTS.md committed with consistency fixes, CLAUDE.md committed as deprecation stub.
